# @aszura/marram-node

> Marram API client for server-side JavaScript (Node.js 20+, Deno, Bun, edge workers). Connects
> end users' third-party accounts, calls those providers' APIs through Marram, manages provider
> webhooks, and signs users in with OAuth2. Holds the secret API key: server-side only.

This file is for AI coding assistants. Follow the rules first; the reference follows.

## Rules

1. **Server only.** `new Marram({ apiKey })` takes the secret key. Never import this package in
   browser or mobile code; use `@aszura/marram-browser` there, with a token your server mints.
2. **Connections belong to your user ID.** `connections.init` requires `externalUserId` — your own
   opaque ID for the user — and every later proxy, refresh, revoke and webhook call addresses the
   connection with that same ID. There is no Marram key to persist. Reconnecting the same user
   replaces their connection.
3. **PKCE on every connect and sign-in.** `connections.init` / `sessions.init` take a
   `codeChallenge`; `claim` needs the matching `codeVerifier`, the `claimCode` query parameter
   the redirect arrived with — and for connections the `flowId` init returned. The connection or
   session is not live until claimed. Keep the flowId and verifier together where only the
   starting user's browser reaches them (their server session, or the browser's `sessionStorage`
   via `@aszura/marram-browser`). A connect redirect carries `?status=connected&claimCode=…` —
   never a key. The `claimCode` is one-time and exists only in that redirect, so a flow can only be
   claimed from it.
4. **Claim once.** `claim` is single-use and expires 30 minutes after the provider step. Delete the
   stored verifier before or right after claiming.
5. **Set `auth`, `redirectUrl` and the provider on the server.** If the browser picks a provider,
   check it against an allowlist.
6. **Branch on `error.code`, never `error.message`.** Unknown codes: fall back to `error.status`.
7. **Proxy responses are the provider's.** `proxy.fetch` returns a `Response` for every provider
   status (4xx/5xx included). Check `response.ok` yourself. Only Marram's own refusals throw.
   The body streams (no size limit) and is **not signed**: don't run `verifyResponse` on it.
8. **Verify webhooks with the raw body**, before any JSON parsing. A re-serialized body won't verify.
9. **Finish endpoint for `@aszura/marram-browser`? Use `connectFlow` / `signInFlow`.** Their
   `finish` handlers serve a sign-in, or a connect started with `claim: 'server'`, with Express and
   web-standard (`Request` → `Response`) handlers. Don't store the provider in a session: the
   browser sends it with the finish payload. The package no longer calls their `start` handlers,
   which remain for browser code you write yourself.
10. **The browser package starts every flow with a token.** `marram.connectToken({ externalUserId })` /
    `marram.signInToken()` (needs `signingSecret` in the client options) mint a short-lived
    token locally — no API call — and the browser runs the flow directly against Marram with
    `connect(provider, { token })` / `signIn(provider, { token })`. One token starts exactly one
    flow, does one browser `disconnect`, or starts one browser `setUpWebhook` (manual webhook
    setup); it can still claim its flow after it expires. Pass
    `redirectUrl` when minting (no dashboard setup needed); without it the page's URL
    must be on the environment's redirect allowlist, and a set allowlist binds the token's URL too.
    Don't sign a URL taken from the browser unchecked. Sign-in claims always stay on your server
    with the API key.

## Install and create a client

```ts
// npm install @aszura/marram-node
import { Marram } from '@aszura/marram-node';

const marram = new Marram({
  apiKey: process.env.MARRAM_API_KEY!,
  // environment: 'staging',            // default 'production'
  // baseUrl: 'https://…/v1',            // overrides environment; include /v1
  // signingSecret: process.env.MARRAM_SIGNING_SECRET, // for connectToken()/signInToken()
  // fetch: customFetch,                 // default globalThis.fetch
});
```

Base URLs: production `https://api.marram.dev/v1`, staging `https://api-staging.marram.dev/v1`
(exported as `BASE_URLS`).

## Connect a user's account (server-side PKCE)

```ts
import { createPkce, parseConnectionRedirect } from '@aszura/marram-node';

// Start, e.g. POST /connect/google, behind your login:
const pkce = await createPkce();
const { flowId, authorizationUrl } = await marram.connections.init('google', {
  auth: 'oAuth2',
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected',
  codeChallenge: pkce.codeChallenge,
  codeChallengeMethod: pkce.codeChallengeMethod, // 'S256'
  externalUserId: user.id,                       // required: your opaque user id
});
req.session.marramConnect = { flowId, codeVerifier: pkce.codeVerifier };
res.redirect(authorizationUrl);

// Return, GET /connected (lands with ?status=connected&claimCode=…), same browser session:
const result = parseConnectionRedirect(fullRequestUrl);
const pendingFlow = req.session.marramConnect;
delete req.session.marramConnect;
if (result.ok && pendingFlow) {
  const connection = await marram.connections.claim('google', pendingFlow.flowId, pendingFlow.codeVerifier, result.claimCode);
  await db.markConnected(user.id, connection.providerKey); // address it by user.id from now on
} else if (!result.ok) {
  // result.error, result.errorMessage: user declined or provider failed
}
```

## Serve `@aszura/marram-browser` (browser-side PKCE)

The browser package starts flows with a token you mint (below). A sign-in, or a connect started
with `claim: 'server'`, also needs a finish endpoint; mount `connectFlow` / `signInFlow`'s `finish`
rather than writing it. Their `start` handlers remain for browser code you write yourself.

```ts
import { Marram, connectFlow, signInFlow } from '@aszura/marram-node';

const connect = connectFlow(marram, {
  providers: ['google', 'trello'],          // allowlist; or { trello: { integrationKey: '…', auth: 'oAuth1' } }
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected', // or (provider) => string
  // auth: 'oAuth2', theme: 'light' | 'dark'
});

// Express / Next.js API routes (after express.json() and your login middleware):
app.post('/marram/start', requireLogin, connect.express.start((req) => ({ externalUserId: req.user.id })));
app.post('/marram/finish', requireLogin, connect.express.finish(async ({ connection }, req) => {
  await db.markConnected(req.user.id, connection.providerKey);
  return { connected: true };               // answered as JSON; undefined answers { ok: true }
}));

// Next.js App Router / Remix / Hono / SvelteKit / Workers (Request in, Response out):
export const POST = connect.web.start(async (request) => ({ externalUserId: (await currentUser(request)).id }));
export const POST = connect.web.finish(async ({ connection }, request) => { /* save; may throw a Response */ });

// Any framework:
const started = await connect.start(req.body, { externalUserId }); // { provider, flowId, authorizationUrl }
const claimed = await connect.finish(req.body);                    // { provider, flowId, connection }
```

`connectFlow.start` requires `externalUserId` in its init (the connection's identity) and refuses
to start without one. `signInFlow(marram, options)` is the same for sign-in: start answers
`{ provider, sessionKey, authorizationUrl }`, finish gives `{ provider, sessionKey, user, raw }`.

Input: start takes `{ provider, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256' }`, finish takes
`{ provider, flowId | sessionKey, codeVerifier, claimCode }`, exactly what the browser package sends.
Bad input throws `FlowInputError` (`status` 400, `code` `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` | `INVALID_INPUT`).
The handlers answer `{ code, error, requestId? }`: 400 for bad input or a claim Marram refused
(`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH`, `MISSING_PKCE_PARAMETERS`,
`CLAIM_CODE_MISMATCH`, `MISSING_CLAIM_CODE`),
502 for any other `MarramError`; anything else goes to `next(error)` / rethrows.
`flowErrorReply(error)` gives that `{ status, body }` (or null) for your own handlers.
`connect.providers` lists the allowlist.

## Sign users in

```ts
const pkce = await createPkce();
const { sessionKey, authorizationUrl } = await marram.sessions.init('google', {
  auth: 'oAuth2',
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/signed-in',
  codeChallenge: pkce.codeChallenge,
  codeChallengeMethod: 'S256',
});
req.session.marram = { sessionKey, codeVerifier: pkce.codeVerifier };
// redirect to authorizationUrl, then at /signed-in?sessionKey=…&claimCode=…:
const pending = req.session.marram;
delete req.session.marram;
const { user, raw } = await marram.sessions.claim('google', pending.sessionKey, pending.codeVerifier, String(req.query.claimCode));
```

## Connect from the browser with a token

```ts
// Your server, when the user clicks:
const { token, jti } = await marram.connectToken({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected', // wins over anything the page sends
});
// Optional restrictions: { provider: 'google', integrationKey: '…', expiresIn: 600 (the default and max; over 600 throws) }
// Sign-in: const { token } = await marram.signInToken(); // sub optional

// The browser (see @aszura/marram-browser): connect('google', { token }) → finish()
```

The token is a 10-minute HS256 JWT signed with your signing secret; the claim's response echoes
its `jti` so you can match results to the token you issued. `mintConnectToken({...})` is the
standalone signer when you don't have a client.

## Call a provider's API

```ts
const response = await marram.proxy.fetch('trello', '1/members/me/boards', { externalUserId: user.id });
if (!response.ok) { /* provider error: inspect response.status / body */ }
const boards = await response.json();

await marram.proxy.fetch('github', 'repos/acme/app/issues', {
  externalUserId: user.id,
  method: 'POST',
  body: { title: 'Bug' },          // sent as JSON
  query: { per_page: '50' },
  headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json' },
  // contentType: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded', // format the provider receives
  // version: '2022-11-28',        // pin provider API version
  // integrationKey: '…',          // only if the provider has several integrations and no default
});
```

`path` is the provider's API path, without a leading host. It must be non-empty and contain no
`..` segment. Caller headers starting with `x-marram-` are dropped.

Async: `await marram.proxy.enqueue(provider, path, { externalUserId, callbackUrl })` returns
`{ requestId }` (HTTP 202). The provider's response is POSTed to `callbackUrl` (public HTTPS).
Verify that callback with `verifyWebhook`.

## Webhooks

```ts
import { verifyWebhook } from '@aszura/marram-node';

// Express: app.post('/hooks/marram', express.raw({ type: '*/*' }), handler)
const valid = await verifyWebhook(req.headers, req.body /* Buffer/raw string */, process.env.MARRAM_SIGNING_SECRET!);
if (!valid) return res.sendStatus(401);
const event = JSON.parse(req.body.toString());
```

`secrets` may be an array during secret rotation. Default timestamp tolerance is 300 s
(`{ toleranceSeconds }` to change). `verifyWebhook` never throws; it returns false.

Manage subscriptions on a connection:

```ts
await marram.webhooks.register('github', { externalUserId, kind: 'push', metadata: 'repo-42', body: { /* kind-specific */ } });
await marram.webhooks.list('github', { externalUserId });
await marram.webhooks.get('github', webhookKey, { externalUserId });
await marram.webhooks.update('github', webhookKey, { externalUserId, body: { … } });
await marram.webhooks.delete('github', webhookKey, { externalUserId });
const { ingressUrl, setupUrl } = await marram.webhooks.initManual('stripe', { externalUserId, redirectUrl });
```

`delete` answers `unregisteredAtProvider`: `false` for a manual webhook or one whose connection was
revoked, which Marram clears without calling the provider. The provider may still hold it; remove
it in the provider's dashboard. Revoking or disconnecting a user leaves their webhooks running until
you delete them. The browser SDK's `setUpWebhook` starts a manual setup with a connect token (Marram
picks the `webhookKey`); `initManual` is the API-key form, needed for a custom key or metadata.

## API reference

All methods are async and throw `MarramError` on a Marram error. `provider` is the provider key,
e.g. `'google'`. The optional `integrationKey` is only needed when a provider has several
integrations and no default.

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `connections.init(provider, { auth, redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256', externalUserId, theme?: 'light' \| 'dark' }, { integrationKey? })` | `{ flowId, authorizationUrl, message? }` |
| `connections.claim(provider, flowId, codeVerifier, claimCode)` | `Connection` |
| `connections.refresh(provider, externalUserId, { integrationKey? })` | `Connection` (throws `CONFLICT` if a refresh is running) |
| `connections.revoke(provider, externalUserId, { integrationKey? })` | `void`. The browser SDK's `disconnect` does this with a connect token, for the token's own user. The user's webhooks keep running until deleted |
| `connections.get(provider, externalUserId, { integrationKey? })` | `Connection` (no refresh, no provider call; throws `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` or `CONNECTION_REVOKED`) |
| `connections.list(provider, { integrationKey })` | `Connection[]` |
| `connectToken({ externalUserId, redirectUrl?, provider?, integrationKey?, expiresIn? })` | `{ token, jti, expiresAt }` (local; needs `signingSecret`) |
| `signInToken({ externalUserId?, redirectUrl?, provider?, integrationKey?, expiresIn? }?)` | `{ token, jti, expiresAt }` (local; needs `signingSecret`) |
| `sessions.init(provider, { auth: 'oAuth2', redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod, externalUserId?, theme? }, { integrationKey? })` | `{ sessionKey, authorizationUrl, message? }` |
| `sessions.claim(provider, sessionKey, codeVerifier, claimCode)` | `UserInfo` `{ user, raw, jti? }` |
| `sessions.userinfo(provider, sessionKey, { integrationKey? })` | `UserInfo` (live from provider) |
| `sessions.refresh(provider, sessionKey)` | `Session` |
| `sessions.revoke(provider, sessionKey, { integrationKey? })` | `void` |
| `sessions.get(provider, sessionKey)` | `Session` (no refresh, no provider call; throws `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` or `SESSION_REVOKED`) |
| `sessions.list(provider, { integrationKey? })` | `Session[]` |
| `proxy.fetch(provider, path, ProxyRequest)` | `Response` (any provider status) |
| `proxy.enqueue(provider, path, ProxyRequest & { callbackUrl })` | `{ requestId }` |
| `webhooks.register(provider, { externalUserId, kind?, webhookKey?, metadata?, version?, body?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, providerWebhookId?, kind? }` |
| `webhooks.list(provider, { externalUserId, integrationKey? })` | `Webhook[]` |
| `webhooks.get(provider, webhookKey, { externalUserId, integrationKey? })` | `Webhook` |
| `webhooks.update(provider, webhookKey, { externalUserId, body?, version?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, … }` |
| `webhooks.delete(provider, webhookKey, { externalUserId, version?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, unregisteredAtProvider, … }` |
| `webhooks.initManual(provider, { externalUserId, redirectUrl?, integrationKey? })` | `{ sessionId, webhookKey, setupUrl, ingressUrl, status: 'pending', fields }`. The browser SDK's `setUpWebhook` does this with a connect token |
| `environment.integrations()` | `Integration[]` |
| `environment.identityProviders()` | `IdentityProvider[]` — enabled for sign-in, filtered by release status. The browser SDK's `listIdentityProviders` fetches a trimmed list with a sign-in token |
| `environment.providers({ externalUserId? })` | `ConnectableProvider[]` — what a user can connect; with `externalUserId`, each integration's `connected`/`connectionStatus` is that user's, else null. The browser SDK's `listProviders` fetches the same list with a connect token |

Browser-flow exports: `connectFlow(marram, { providers, redirectUrl, auth?, theme? })` and
`signInFlow(...)` → `Flow` with `start(input, { externalUserId? })`, `finish(input)`,
`express.start(init?)`, `express.finish(onClaimed)`, `web.start(init?)`, `web.finish(onClaimed)`,
`providers`; `FlowInputError` (`status: 400`, `code`); `flowErrorReply(error)` → `{ status, body } | null`.

Standalone exports: `createPkce()` → `{ codeVerifier, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256' }`;
`parseConnectionRedirect(url)` → `{ ok: true, claimCode } | { ok: false, error, errorMessage }`
(`error` is `'missing_status'` when the URL carries neither `status=connected` nor `error`,
`'missing_claim_code'` when a connected redirect has no `claimCode`);
`mintConnectToken({ use, organizationId, environmentId, signingSecret, externalUserId?, … })`;
`verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, secrets, opts?)`; `verifyResponse(response, secrets, opts?)`;
`verifySignature({ body, timestamp, signature, secrets, toleranceSeconds? })`.

Types: `Connection`, `Session`, `Webhook`, `Integration`, `IdentityProvider`, `UserInfo`,
`FormField`, `AuthType` (`oAuth1 | oAuth2 | api_key | basic | session`), `CredentialStatus`
(`active | pending | reauth_required | error | revoked | inactive`), `ProxyRequest`,
`MarramOptions`.

## Errors

```ts
import { MarramError } from '@aszura/marram-node';

try {
  await marram.connections.refresh('google', externalUserId);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof MarramError) {
    error.status;    // HTTP status
    error.code;      // stable code; `HTTP_<status>` if none was sent
    error.requestId; // quote in support requests
    error.body;      // parsed JSON or raw text
  }
}
```

Common codes: `INVALID_API_KEY`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RATE_LIMITED`,
`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `CONFLICT` (refresh already running; retry shortly), `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND`,
`INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND`, `INTEGRATION_KEY_REQUIRED` (pass `integrationKey`),
`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND`, `MISSING_EXTERNAL_USER_ID`,
`MISSING_FLOW_ID`, `MISSING_PKCE_PARAMETERS`,
`CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH` (wrong or reused verifier; start again), `AUTH_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`,
`BLOCKED_PATH`; token flows add `INVALID_CONNECT_TOKEN`, `CONNECT_TOKEN_EXPIRED`,
`CONNECT_TOKEN_REUSED`, `CONNECT_TOKEN_WRONG_USE`, `REDIRECT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED`. The full list is
in `openapi.yaml` under `components.schemas.Error`.
